title: High-Protein, Low-Calorie Foods: Protein per 100 Calories

seo.title: High-Protein, Low-Calorie Foods
seo.meta_description: Compare lean fish, egg whites, turkey, chicken and high-protein dairy by grams of protein per 100 calories and realistic serving.
seo.search_intent: Find protein-dense foods with relatively few calories.

excerpt: Lean fish, egg whites, turkey breast, chicken breast and low-fat high-protein dairy provide large amounts of protein for relatively few calories.
content_html:
A food can be high in protein per 100 grams and still be calorie-dense. Aged cheese, nuts and seeds are good examples. When the question is how much protein you get for a fixed amount of energy, lean fish, egg whites and poultry move toward the top.

Protein per 100 calories

FoodProtein/100 gCalories/100 gProtein/100 cal
Cooked yellowfin tuna29.2 g13022.4 g
Cooked cod22.8 g10521.7 g
Egg whites10.9 g5221.0 g
Cooked turkey breast29.5 g14520.3 g
Cooked chicken breast31.0 g16518.8 g
Plain nonfat Greek yogurt~10 g~59~17 g
Low-fat cottage cheese~11.5 g~85~13.5 g
Firm tofu~15 g~145~10.3 g
Cooked lentils9.0 g1167.8 g

Lean fish

Yellowfin tuna provides about 29.2 g protein for 130 calories per 100 g. Cod provides 22.8 g for 105 calories. Chicken breast contains more protein by weight than cod —31 versus 22.8 g— but also more calories —165 versus 105— so cod provides slightly more protein per calorie.

Egg whites

Egg whites provide about 10.9 g protein and 52 calories/100 g, while whole egg is around 12.6 g protein and 143 calories. The yolk adds fat, choline and many vitamins and minerals, so higher protein efficiency comes with a different nutrient profile.

Turkey and chicken

Cooked turkey breast is about 29.5 g protein and 145 calories/100 g; chicken breast about 31 g and 165 calories. A 5-ounce / 142 g serving gives roughly 42 g protein and 206 calories from turkey versus 44 g and 234 calories from chicken.

High-protein dairy

Plain nonfat Greek yogurt can provide around 10 g protein and 59 calories/100 g. A 6-ounce / 170 g container is therefore around 17 g protein and 100 calories. Labels vary substantially across Greek-style, skyr and protein yogurts.

Plant options

Firm tofu, seitan and soy foods provide more protein per calorie than most nuts and seeds. Lentils supply 9 g protein and 116 calories/100 g, less protein efficiency than cod but nearly 8 g fiber.

Almonds provide around 21.2 g protein but roughly 579 calories/100 g, compared with 22.8 g and 105 calories for cod. Almonds add fiber, vitamin E, magnesium and unsaturated fat, which the protein-per-calorie number does not measure.

Serving comparison

FoodServingProteinCalories
Cod5 oz / 142 g32 g149
Turkey breast5 oz / 142 g42 g206
Chicken breast5 oz / 142 g44 g234
Nonfat Greek yogurt6 oz / 170 g~17 g~100
Cooked lentils1 cup / ~200 g18 g232

What the metric does and does not tell you

Protein per calorie is useful when total energy is limited, but it does not score fiber, essential fats, vitamins or minerals. Salmon provides less protein per calorie than cod because it contains more fat, yet that fat includes EPA and DHA omega-3s.

Bottom line

Lean fish, egg whites, turkey, chicken and nonfat high-protein dairy are especially efficient ways to add protein without many calories. Plant foods and fatty fish may rank lower on this one measure while contributing nutrients the ranking does not capture.

Sources

Composition values come from USDA FoodData Central.

faq.question: What foods give the most protein for the fewest calories?
faq.answer: Lean tuna, cod, egg whites and turkey breast are among the most efficient common foods.

faq.question: Is chicken more protein-dense than fish?
faq.answer: By weight, chicken breast is higher than cod, 31 versus 22.8 g/100 g. Per calorie, cod is slightly more efficient because it has only about 105 calories/100 g.

faq.question: Are lentils low in protein?
faq.answer: No. One cup near 200 g provides about 18 g protein plus roughly 15–16 g fiber.
